Fidelity

/fih-DEL-ih-tee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Fidelity means continued faithfulness or loyalty to a person, cause, promise, or original source.

Fidelity means continued faithfulness or loyalty to a person, cause, promise, or original source. Even after a giant discount store opened across the highway, Mr. Abara's fidelity to the family-owned hardware shop where he had traded for thirty years never wavered.

Worked Example

The translator's fidelity to the original poem meant keeping its plain, quiet tone, even when flashier English words were available.

Here fidelity is faithfulness to an original source: the translator stays true to what the poem actually is instead of 'improving' it. Loyalty to a person and faithfulness to an original are two faces of the same word.

How Fidelity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

loyalty

loyalty: faithful support for a person or cause

allegiance

allegiance: committed loyalty, often to a group or country

constancy

constancy: steadiness that does not change over time

Antonyms

betrayal

betrayal: breaking someone's trust

disloyalty

disloyalty: failure to stand by a person or cause

How Strong Is It? — attachment → fidelity → devotion

attachment vs. fidelity

attachment vs. fidelity: Attachment is weaker than fidelity — you can feel attached to a place or person without ever being tested; fidelity is loyalty that holds up over time and through difficulty.

devotion vs. fidelity

devotion vs. fidelity: Devotion is stronger than fidelity — devotion is all-consuming commitment, the kind that reorganizes your whole life around the person or cause you serve.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — fidel

Root — fidel: faithful (Latin fidelis, from fides, 'faith, trust')

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: the state or quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Fidelity is literally 'the state of being faithful.' The Latin root fides, 'faith or trust,' sits inside a whole family of English words about trusting and being trusted.

Use the root in a new word: bona fide

Use the root in a new word: bona fide: The signed letter from the artist proved the painting was a bona fide original — literally 'in good faith' — and not a clever copy.

Word Choice

Formal — warm, serious register

Fidelity is loyalty proven over time — to a person, a promise, a cause, or an original source (a translator's fidelity to a text). Bonus sense: 'high fidelity' audio describes a recording that stays faithful to the original sound. Don't confuse it with affinity, another word in this unit: affinity is a spontaneous liking that can spark in a single moment, while fidelity is faithfulness sustained across months and years.
